scope: 120 FPS runtime diagnosis after the desktop restart: traced vs untraced throughput, cursor-only path, stall structure, bottleneck attribution limits

app_process.renderer_thread: Thread-8 (20654) owns CopyBatch/Draw/eglSwapBuffers on the SurfaceView

runtime.activating_earlier_limitation: resolved; the X11 display clock is live 120 and no longer the startup default

android_display.note: mode 2 is 144 Hz but has not been evaluated; only mode 1 was active

traced_diagnosis.tooling: atrace (gfx,view,sched; 8 MB buffer; -a com.termux.x11) plus profile-display SurfaceFlinger sampling

server_markers_from_atrace.choreographer_callback_distribution: bimodal, 8.3 ms bursts mixed with ~25 ms intervals

system_cpu.interpretation: no CPU saturation; X server and renderer threads were mostly blocked, not running

cursor_only_path.method: xdotool mousemove chain (single client), ~118 moves/s, SurfaceFlinger --latency delta on the X11 SurfaceView layer

idle_window.note: window contained concurrent activity from the running desktop client, not an empty desktop

motion_window.note: SurfaceFlinger keeps only the last 127 frames, so the visible span (about 1.07 s) is a lower bound of motion-time presents

attribution.gpu: not the bottleneck: GPU-copy batch p50 2.06 ms including fence, eglSwapBuffers p50 0.57 ms, GPU-ready waits below 0.1 ms, GPU frequency stayed between 104.45 and 441.6 MHz
attribution.cpu: not saturated in the sampled windows
attribution.measurement_effect: the same 640x480 workload measured about 38-40 fps under atrace plus SurfaceFlinger polling and about 80-83 fps untraced; traced numbers describe a traced condition, not normal use
attribution.remaining_gap: about 46 percent of untraced frames need more than one vsync; roughly every 6 to 9 frames stalls for 25-30 ms, which pulls the average from a 117-118 fps median down to 76-80 fps
attribution.stall_source: not attributed; candidates are the serialized X11 present loop (client copy -> server tick -> renderer draw/swap -> SurfaceFlinger), the periodic empty redraws, and contention with the concurrently running desktop client

conclusions: 120 FPS is active and effective at runtime: X11 -max-fps 120, root display clock [1, 120, 15], SurfaceFlinger layer period 8.333 ms, and median presents of 8.4-8.6 ms in unthrottled windows
no hardware ceiling has been demonstrated: three concurrent clients submitted 257.6 fps in total on the same display path
the earlier 38-40 fps figures were taken under tracing and must not be read as normal-use throughput
the remaining gap to 120 fps is a stall tail, not a uniform per-frame cost
cursor-only motion already presents at roughly one vsync per frame; its cost is CPU and full-surface redraw work, not frame pacing
limitations: No power, energy, or battery-life measurement
No per-window SurfaceFlinger attribution: the X11 desktop presents as a single SurfaceView layer
The desktop was running a heavy client during sampling; idle and stall numbers mix that client's work
The 3-client aggregate counts submitted copies, not distinct displayed frames
Stall source is not yet isolated; traced and untraced conditions are both recorded and are not interchangeable
144 Hz mode is supported by the panel but was not evaluated
